# CIS Tax Refund Estimator (UK)

> Free, client-side web tool for UK self-employed construction subcontractors under the Construction Industry Scheme (CIS). It estimates Income Tax (rest of UK or Scottish bands), Class 2 and Class 4 National Insurance and student loan repayments on self-employed profit plus any PAYE wages, for 2025/26 or 2026/27, and compares that with CIS deductions and tax already paid to give an estimated refund or amount owed. It also shows which SA103S/SA103F boxes the figures go in and whether payments on account are likely. Estimate only, not tax advice.

Key facts (from GOV.UK, last checked 6 October 2026):

- Refund = CIS deducted + PAYE tax + loan repayments already taken − (Income Tax + Class 4 + Class 2 + student loan due). Sole traders claim it through Self Assessment after 5 April; HMRC refunds any overpayment.
- Turnover is the gross amount before CIS deductions, including materials charged (SA103S box 9 / SA103F box 15). CIS deductions go in SA103S box 38 / SA103F box 81 (2025/26 forms). Materials: box 11 / 17. Car, van and travel: box 12 / 20.
- Personal Allowance £12,570 (2025/26 and 2026/27), reduced by £1 for every £2 over £100,000. Basic rate 20% on the first £37,700 of taxable income, 40% to £125,140, 45% above.
- Scotland 2026/27 (taxable income after allowance): 19% to £3,967, 20% to £16,956, 21% to £31,092, 42% to £62,430, 45% to £125,140, 48% above. 2025/26: £2,827 / £14,921 / £31,092 / £62,430 / £125,140.
- Class 4 NI: 6% on profits £12,570 to £50,270, 2% above (both years). Class 2: treated as paid if profits are at least £6,845 (2025/26) or £7,105 (2026/27); voluntary £3.50 or £3.65 a week below that.
- Simplified mileage for cars and vans: 55p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in 2026/27 (backdated to 6 April 2026; 45p before), then 25p.
- Student loans via Self Assessment: 9% of total income above Plan 1 £26,900 / Plan 2 £29,385 / Plan 4 £33,795 / Plan 5 £25,000 (2026/27); 2025/26: £26,065 / £28,470 / £32,745 (no Plan 5 repayments before April 2026). Postgraduate Loan 6% above £21,000.
- Payments on account are not needed if less than £1,000 is owed through Self Assessment or more than 80% of the tax was collected at source (CIS deductions count).
- Example (England, 2026/27): £40,000 gross, £6,400 CIS deducted, £14,000 expenses → £26,000 profit, £2,686.00 Income Tax, £805.80 Class 4, estimated refund £2,908.20.
